@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+# Pieces
+
+1. Define the new public day-book entry shape and its invariant.  Replace the
+   identity-bearing `who` value in every entry with a stable person number
+   (for example `person_id`), while retaining `day`, `kind`, and `note`.
+   Establish that no value in the JSON book may identify a person, rather than
+   merely changing the field's display label.  This is the contract shared by
+   `book.py`, `door.py`, `tally.py`, and the CLI.
+
+2. Introduce a clerk-only roll as a separate persistence boundary.  It must
+   resolve a person as entered at the door to their stable number, and resolve
+   a number back to a person for clerk-facing commands.  It must have its own
+   path/configuration and load/save functions, and must not be added as a key
+   to the `Book` dictionary or written by `book.save`; today `Book` is the
+   entire JSON document and `book.save` serializes it wholesale.
+
+3. Change new-entry recording in `door.py`.  Make `give` and `refuse` receive
+   a person number (or a value resolved to one before they are called) and
+   append that number instead of the supplied name.  Preserve their existing
+   dole-table validation, refusal-kind encoding (`refused-<kind>`), and
+   required-refusal-note rule.  Update their docstrings and type/interface
+   names so the door boundary no longer claims it writes names into the book.
+
+4. Adapt the clerk workflow in `cli.py`.  The `give` and `refuse` commands
+   should accept the clerk's person input and use the private roll to obtain
+   the stable number before calling `door`; they must save the roll if a
+   numbering/registration operation changes it, separately from saving the
+   book.  The `history` command should translate its clerk-facing person input
+   to a number before querying.  `day` and `often` must use the numbers held
+   in the book, with any name presentation performed only after lookup in the
+   private roll.  This keeps CLI output useful to the clerk without putting a
+   name back into `book.json`; decide whether a visitor-safe numeric display
+   mode is needed as part of the command design.
+
+5. Change read-side tally semantics.  `tally.history` should match a person
+   number, and `tally.often` should count by person number; `helped` can
+   continue filtering entries by day but its consumers must treat its identity
+   field as numeric.  Update the docstrings, parameter names, and return-value
+   expectations so none of the reporting layer describes the book as naming
+   people.
+
+6. Migrate the existing book before it is exposed.  Load the current entries,
+   allocate or look up one stable number for each distinct existing exact
+   `who` string, write that correspondence only to the separate roll, replace
+   each historical `who` in the book with its number, and save the sanitized
+   book.  The migration must cover gifts and refusals alike because both are
+   ordinary entries and both are selected by `tally`.  Include a pre-write
+   validation pass that rejects any entry without a resolvable identity and a
+   post-write scan/assertion that the public JSON has no old `who` fields or
+   person-name values.  Make the process safely repeatable or explicitly
+   one-shot, with backup/rollback handling chosen before overwriting the only
+   existing record.
+
+7. Revise the README and add automated coverage.  Replace examples that put
+   names directly in `book.json` with the new clerk workflow, document that
+   the roll is separate and sensitive, and state the public-book schema.
+   Tests should cover new gifts/refusals, repeat lookup of the same person,
+   history and counts, day reporting, persistence of both stores, migration
+   of mixed historical entries, and an assertion that the serialized book
+   contains identifiers but no names/roll data.  There is currently no test
+   suite in the repository, so selecting its framework and test command is
+   part of this work.
+
+# Order and dependencies
+
+1. Settle the identifier and private-roll contract first (Pieces 1–2).  The
+   present `Book = dict[str, Any]`, `book.load`, and `book.save` provide no
+   schema enforcement and write the whole dictionary, so the storage boundary
+   must be clear before implementation can prevent accidental roll inclusion.
+
+2. Build and test the private roll and public entry contract next (Pieces 1–2,
+   plus the relevant part of Piece 7).  Both the ongoing write path and the
+   historical conversion need a consistent name-to-number allocation.
+
+3. Update the write and read libraries together (Pieces 3 and 5).  `door.give`
+   and `door.refuse` currently append `who`, while `tally.history` and
+   `tally.often` read exactly that key.  Changing only one side would leave
+   newly written entries unreadable or reports keyed by the old schema.
+
+4. Wire the CLI after those APIs are known (Piece 4).  `cli.py` is the only
+   supplied caller of `door` and `tally`, loads the book once, and saves after
+   mutating commands; it is therefore where separate roll lifecycle and any
+   clerk-only name resolution must be coordinated.
+
+5. Run the historical migration only after the new roll and number-based paths
+   have been validated (Piece 6).  Its output must be consumable immediately
+   by the updated `tally` and CLI, and it overwrites the pre-existing public
+   record.
+
+6. Finish documentation and full regression/migration checks last (Piece 7),
+   once command syntax, roll location, and migration behavior have been
+   decided.  The privacy scan should also be a release gate for the migrated
+   `book.json`.
+
+# Open questions and risks
+
+- The repository does not say what constitutes a person for matching: exact
+  spelling (the current behavior), a clerk-issued number, or a normalized
+  name.  Choosing normalization can merge distinct people; retaining exact
+  strings can create duplicate roll records.
+
+- It does not define the number format, whether numbers may be reused, or how
+  the next number is assigned.  Stable, never-reused opaque identifiers are
+  the natural privacy-preserving default, but that is a policy decision.
+
+- “Kept apart” and “the clerk's alone” do not specify the roll's required
+  storage location, file permissions, encryption, backups, access controls,
+  or whether it may be passed with `--book`.  A separate JSON file alone
+  prevents inclusion in the public book but may not meet the intended access
+  control standard.
+
+- Existing names may appear outside `who`: free-text `note` is copied without
+  validation, and the current repository gives examples of a surname in a
+  note.  The requirement says the whole book is to name no one, but the code
+  cannot determine whether each note identifies someone.  Trustees must set a
+  redaction policy and provide/approve review of historical and future notes;
+  automated structural migration alone cannot guarantee this.
+
+- The migration's source data is not present in the repository.  Its size,
+  malformed entries, duplicate/ambiguous names, and operational backup
+  requirements are unknown.  A dry-run report and a recoverable backup or
+  transaction plan should be agreed before modifying the live file.
+
+- The intended audience for `day`, `history`, and `often` is unclear.  Current
+  output prints names for day and often, whereas a visitor may be allowed to
+  see only numbers; a clerk may need names resolved from the private roll.
+  This determines whether to split commands, add an explicit private-output
+  mode, or make all reports numeric.
+
+- There are no tests, packaging metadata, or declared compatibility policy.
+  The plan cannot establish the supported Python version, test runner, or
+  whether callers outside `cli.py` depend on the existing `door`/`tally`
+  function signatures.

+# Pieces
+
+1. Define the log reader's result for an unparseable non-blank physical
+   line in `log.py`.  At present `read()` promises `list[Line]` and calls
+   `json.loads` in a comprehension, so invalid JSON, a valid non-object JSON
+   value, or an object missing fields can escape as an exception or later
+   break a reckoning.  Introduce an explicit representation for a rejected
+   line that retains its original text (and preferably line number and
+   reason), separately from a valid `Line`.  Decide the minimum structural
+   validation required for a line to be a working: the readers in
+   `reckon.py` require `day`, `working`, and `quarters`, while preservation
+   and month filtering also depend on knowing how to treat `day`.
+
+2. Make the shared log-reading path tolerant and auditable.  Replace the
+   all-or-nothing list comprehension with line-by-line decoding and
+   validation: valid workings go to the usable entries, rejected lines go to
+   the explicit set-aside collection unchanged.  Blank lines need an
+   intentional policy too, since the current reader silently ignores them.
+   Expose the rejected-line accounting to callers instead of merely catching
+   `JSONDecodeError`; otherwise `reckon` would continue but the bad record
+   would again be silently dropped.
+
+3. Adapt `reckon.day` and `reckon.standing` to consume only valid workings
+   from that shared result, without inventing values for damaged records.
+   Preserve their current aggregates for valid lines and give their callers a
+   way to learn that the result excluded set-aside records (for example a
+   richer return/result object, or a companion reporting API).  Update
+   `cli.py`'s `day` and `standing` commands to present that accounting in the
+   chosen interface, so a steward is not told a partial figure as if it were
+   complete.
+
+4. Centralize lossless whole-file handling in `log.py`.  Replace the direct
+   `open(..., "w")` implementation of `rewrite()` with a transaction-like
+   write: construct the complete replacement in a temporary file alongside
+   the log, flush and `fsync` it, and atomically replace the old file only
+   after the replacement is ready; clean up a failed temporary file.  Retain
+   the pre-existing file until the commit point, and consider directory sync
+   after replacement if the durability claim includes power loss.  Ensure the
+   API can write a mixture of validated entries and preserved raw rejected
+   records, rather than JSON-reserializing every line.
+
+5. Harden appends in `log.append` to the same preservation invariant.  Check
+   how an append failure is surfaced, make serialization happen before the
+   file is opened/changed, and specify whether a short/failed write leaves a
+   detectable incomplete tail that the tolerant reader will set aside.  The
+   implementation must never truncate or replace old contents while adding a
+   working; a successful append should be fully terminated and durable under
+   the selected durability policy.
+
+6. Rework `monthend.carry` to use the shared lossless reader rather than its
+   own `read_text`/`json.loads` loop.  Sum and lift only valid lines belonging
+   to the requested month.  Keep every other valid line and every set-aside
+   raw line in the replacement file, in original order where possible, then
+   add the generated `carried` line and commit through the safe rewrite path.
+   Return/report the set-aside accounting with the monthly totals so a carry
+   cannot make damaged records invisible.  Remove the duplicate parsing
+   logic once this is done.
+
+7. Add regression and failure-injection tests (there is no existing test
+   suite in the repository, so first establish a standard-library test
+   layout).  Cover malformed JSON, JSON scalars/arrays, malformed but
+   newline-terminated records, a partial final line, and records whose shape
+   is unusable by reckonings.  Verify `day`, `standing`, and `carry` still
+   process the valid records and expose the count/details of set-aside ones.
+   Test that a carry preserves the exact bad bytes and valid non-carried
+   records.  Mock serialization, file writes, flush/fsync, and replacement
+   failures to confirm the original log remains intact whenever the rewrite
+   fails; also test append failure behavior and the normal CLI paths.
+
+# Order and dependencies
+
+1. Establish the valid/rejected record model and its reporting contract
+   first.  It is the shared boundary `reckon.py` is documented to use, and it
+   determines what `monthend.py` can safely preserve and what the CLI must
+   show.
+
+2. Implement and test the tolerant reader next.  Both reckonings currently
+   call `log.read(path)` exclusively, so changing them before that contract
+   exists would either retain the current exceptions or force each consumer
+   to duplicate parsing policy.
+
+3. Design the lossless rewrite representation and atomic commit before
+   changing month-end.  `carry()` is the only current whole-file mutation and
+   currently builds `kept: list[log.Line]`; it cannot retain a rejected raw
+   line unless the writer accepts that representation.
+
+4. Move `monthend.carry` onto the shared reader and safe writer once both
+   exist.  This removes the only direct second parser and closes the current
+   truncation window caused by `open(path, "w")`.
+
+5. Update reckonings and the CLI against the finalized reader/reporting
+   contract.  `cli.py` is the user-facing consumer of their present
+   dictionaries, so changing their return shapes or adding status must be
+   coordinated.
+
+6. Harden append alongside the writer work, then complete cross-module and
+   failure tests.  `floorwork.py` already funnels all three workings through
+   `log.append`, so it should need no separate persistence mechanism; its
+   tests demonstrate that steep, turn, and kiln inherit the invariant.
+
+# Open questions and risks
+
+- “Cannot be made sense of” is not defined precisely.  The repository shows
+  required fields only indirectly, and does not say whether invalid dates,
+  unknown workings (including the generated `carried` entry), non-integer or
+  negative quarters, non-integer places, and extra fields are rejected,
+  preserved-but-ignored, or valid.
+
+- “Set aside and accounted for” does not specify the outward interface:
+  warnings on stderr, fields returned from the library, a sidecar quarantine
+  file, or a distinct CLI command are all plausible.  A sidecar creates a
+  second persistence problem; keeping raw lines in the log is the only
+  approach directly supported by the one-file description, but that choice
+  needs confirmation.
+
+- The meaning of “file holding less than it held before” needs a failure
+  model.  Atomic replacement protects the previous pathname on ordinary
+  write/replace errors, but crashes and power loss require explicit `fsync`
+  guarantees and filesystem assumptions.  Append can also leave newly
+  written partial bytes; that does not lose old bytes but must be classed as
+  a set-aside record on the next read.
+
+- Current month matching is `str(entry["day"]).startswith(month)`, which
+  accepts malformed dates and prefix collisions, while the carried summary
+  uses an artificial `YYYY-MM-99` day.  Tight validation could alter existing
+  carry behavior, so the desired compatibility policy must be settled.
+
+- `carry()` currently reports only valid working totals and appends a
+  zero-quarter `carried` entry.  The repository does not establish whether a
+  later carry should include, ignore, or reject prior carried entries, nor
+  whether set-aside records should block a ledger close.  The plan should not
+  assume either financial policy.

+# Plan: introduce county new pence
+
+## Pieces
+
+1. Define the currency boundary and representation in `roll.py`.  The roll is
+   the only persisted record and currently exposes `{"lines": [...]}` with
+   each `charge` a bare number.  Add a roll-level way to identify the new-pence
+   format (and a migration/normalisation path for an existing, unmarked roll),
+   so `load()` returns a roll whose recorded charges are unambiguously new
+   pence and `save()` preserves that form.  Convert historic stored charges by
+   the exact 5/12 factor (one old penny is 5/12 of a new penny); do not rely on
+   a changed tariff to reinterpret what was actually taken.
+
+2. Establish an exact new-money amount type/rounding policy and conversion
+   helpers at the currency boundary.  Existing `int` annotations and `0`
+   charges assume whole old pence, but the current rates convert to 25/12,
+   5/6, and 5/12 new pence for cart, horse, and foot.  Make the chosen exact
+   representation usable in JSON, summation, comparisons, and display, and
+   retain zero for waved-through crossings.
+
+3. Replace `tariff.py`'s old-pence table and its documentation with new-pence
+   rates, using the shared representation.  Keep `rate()` and `kinds()` as the
+   source of valid crossing kinds, but ensure their result is expressly in new
+   pence.
+
+4. Update `gate.py` to record a new-pence charge in every newly appended line.
+   `cross()` should take the new tariff rate; `wave_through()` remains zero but
+   continues to validate the kind through the new tariff.  Update type hints
+   and docstrings to state the post-Lady-Day unit.
+
+5. Update `till.py` readers.  `takings()` must add the new-money charge values
+   without precision loss, while `misrecorded()` must compare against the new
+   tariff and still accept a zero wave-through.  Its audit description should
+   no longer imply an old-pence integer charge.
+
+6. Update `cli.py` presentation.  Replace the `pence(int)` formatter and its
+   call sites in `takings`, `check`, and `rates` so output labels and formatting
+   identify and correctly render new pence, including any non-whole amounts
+   permitted by the agreed representation.  Preserve `free` for zero.
+
+7. Revise `README.md` and module documentation to describe the roll format,
+   rate unit, examples, and operational meaning of the cutover.  Add or update
+   tests for loading/migrating a pre-cutover roll, recording paid and waved
+   crossings, daily takings, audit behaviour, saved JSON, and each monetary CLI
+   command; include boundary-day cases once the cutover rule is decided.
+
+## Order and dependencies
+
+1. Settle the cutover and fractional-new-pence decisions first.  They determine
+   both the persisted schema and the amount abstraction; changing either later
+   would invalidate the tariff, gate, readers, and CLI work.
+2. Implement and test the amount conversion and `roll.py` migration next.
+   `roll.load()`/`save()` are the sole JSON boundary, and every command loads
+   the roll before dispatch (`cli.py:41`), so this is the only central place to
+   prevent old and new values being mixed in a roll.
+3. Change `tariff.py` after the representation exists.  `gate.cross()` calls
+   `tariff.rate()` directly, and `till.misrecorded()` compares every stored
+   charge to it, so the table cannot safely change independently.
+4. Adapt `gate.py` and `till.py` together against the new table and migrated
+   roll.  Gate writes the four line fields and till is the code that sums and
+   audits those exact fields.
+5. Adapt the CLI once its dependencies return the new value type, then update
+   the README and execute the end-to-end command tests.  This sequencing covers
+   all outputs that presently call `pence()` and avoids documenting provisional
+   display semantics.
+
+## Open questions and risks
+
+- Does “from Lady Day” mean 25 March 1926 (the year used in the examples), 25
+  March in every year, or a separately configured/effective date?  The code
+  treats days only as ISO strings and has no current-date or policy setting.
+- Must existing lines be converted when first read, or must only crossings on
+  and after the effective date be new pence?  The requirement says all tolls
+  written and read back are new pence, but the repository does not state the
+  fate of already-written old-pence rolls.
+- What is the required treatment of fractions?  Exact conversion creates
+  fractional new pence for every current rate.  The repository offers no
+  rounding rule, subunit, decimal notation, or constraint that a charge must
+  remain an integer; silently rounding would change the parish's stated
+  2.4:1 value.
+- If old and new crossings may coexist around the boundary, should the roll
+  retain per-line currency/version metadata, or should the whole file be
+  migrated atomically?  A bare `charge` cannot identify its unit.
+- The repository contains no test suite or sample `roll.json`.  Expected JSON
+  shape for a currency marker, backward-compatibility guarantees, and exact CLI
+  output have to be agreed before tests can lock them down.
